stories.title: Baseline (as is)
stories.what_happened: Nothing has gone wrong yet. This is the plan for the coming year, before any disruption.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It serves 99.45% of demand at a landed cost of €23.36M, moving it in 2,715 truck trips. It clears every governance gate, so it could be released to the factory without anyone signing it off.

stories.title: The road into Venlo closes
stories.what_happened: The motorway into Venlo closes for two weeks, from day 7 to day 21: nothing reaches Grenspoort Cross-dock (3PL), which serves every German customer and holds about a week of their flow.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It filled the cross-dock before the road closed — 18 trucks in the first week, against 15 normally — sent 0 while it was shut, and caught up with 18 in the following three weeks, against 13. Its racking was full at the peak: 190 of 190 pallets, so it could not hold more ahead. Service: 99.43%.

stories.title: A German grocer's promotion order
stories.what_happened: Rheinbogen Frischemarkt, a German grocer delivered through Grenspoort Cross-dock (3PL), places a promotion order for an extra 31k cases of Sparkling Lemonade, due on day 10.
stories.what_the_plan_did: Rheinbogen Frischemarkt were filled at 99.8%. Where capacity ran out, lower-priority accounts went short first: Groothandel Baronie (priority 60) short 2,254 more cases.

takeaways.title: The road into Venlo closes
takeaways.action: It filled the cross-dock before the road closed — 18 trucks in the first week, against 15 normally — sent 0 while it was shut, and caught up with 18 in the following three weeks, against 13.
assumptions: Road closed: day 7 to day 21 of the year.
Found out late: the baseline is kept until day 7, then re-planned as an emergency, the best re-plan possible.
Every plan is proven within ±€128,747 of the best possible; a difference inside that is too small to measure.
Prices, costs and the rest of the year's demand are the baseline's.
takeaways.message: Acting ahead saves 20,973 cases from shortage; the money is too small to measure against the ±€129k the plans are solved to.
takeaways.case: Found out on day 7, the road into Venlo closes makes a profit change too small to measure and service falls to 99.19%. Acting ahead saves 20,973 cases from shortage; the money is too small to measure against the ±€129k the plans are solved to.
calc: Profit a year: baseline €27,009,755; found out on day 7 €26,970,112; acted ahead €27,022,494.
Hit of finding out late = baseline − found out late = €27,009,755 − €26,970,112 = €39,643.
Won back by acting ahead = acted ahead − found out late = €27,022,494 − €26,970,112 = €52,382.
Read against the ±€128,747 the plans are proven to: too small to measure.
Orders served, by value: baseline 99.45%, found out late 99.19%, acted ahead 99.43%.
ahead_costs: Against finding out late, acting ahead brings in revenue +€123k and spends: raw materials and packaging +€46k; production +€12k; warehousing −€482; capital tied up in stock +€1,752; transport, toll included +€11k; carbon price −€15; stock left at year end −€686. Net on profit: +€52k, too small to measure against the ±€129k the plans are solved to.
Average stock carried (working capital): €586k found out late, €601k acting ahead, €15k more; the capital tied up in it costs €1,752 more a year.

Room to store it: the racking acting ahead fills most is Grenspoort Cross-dock (3PL) ambient, at 100% of its 190 pallets at its peak against 94% found out late; it fills Grenspoort Cross-dock (3PL) ambient to the top, no headroom left.
